About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

Your Team, Your Impact

Our team performs the electrical validation of custom Marvell ASICs built around high-speed Ethernet and PCIe IO, the silicon that powers modern data center infrastructure. Day to day, we characterize demanding high-speed measurements on precision instrumentation and scale the Python test automation that makes validation faster and more repeatable. You will join a close-knit group of about eight engineers based on-site in Santa Clara, working at the intersection of high-speed hardware and validation test infrastructure. That work directly enables the products that connect enterprise, cloud, AI, and carrier networks.

What You Can Expect

- Analyze overnight test data and compare results against expected outcomes.
- Set up and calibrate high-speed benches using oscilloscopes, bit error rate testers, network analyzers, and pattern generators.
- Characterize device parameters and document findings in summary reports for your manager.
- Debug unexpected results with your mentor and team until a solution is found.
- Build Python automation and AI-assisted validation agents, using tools such as Claude and Glean, to speed up daily routines.

What We're Looking For

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
- Solid grasp of engineering fundamentals and an understanding of microelectronic circuits and systems
- Knowledge of, or strong interest in, RF systems or high-speed data transmission and signal integrity
- Programming experience in Python, with test automation experience a plus
- Knowledge of electronics and printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) is desired
- Experience with data processing and visualization is desired

28 - 56, $ per hour.

The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today.

Today, the last of the engineers who imagined and built these systems are retiring. As they go, we lose not only the engineering knowledge gained from their decades of imagination and trial-and-error, but also the spirit that made that imagination possible.

Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. By restoring the capability of our antiquated supply chains, we increase the country’s capacity to imagine and realize new systems, and make a physical world that looks very different from today.

Overview

The Electrical Design Engineering Intern works alongside our electrical team to take aerospace hardware from concept toward flight qualification. You will own a scoped electrical design project for the summer, with a dedicated mentor and direct access to the build and test engineers who will bring your work to life.

This is not a shadowing program. Interns at Amca design, build, and debug real hardware. You should expect your schematics and boards to be reviewed with the same rigor as a full-time engineer's, and to have something on the bench before you leave.

Responsibilities

- Design electronics from concept to functional prototype, including hardware selection, PCB design, and system-level integration

- Contribute to the design and prototyping of new electrical hardware

- Support electrical design for flight hardware, including schematic capture, electrical analysis, component selection, and PCBA layout

- Build up early hardware, then iterate quickly based on results

- Run bench testing and basic functional and development tests on the hardware you build

- Debug failures down to root cause and carry the fix back into the design

- Troubleshoot issues that span the system, using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes and digital multimeters

- Select components with attention to de-rating, tolerance, and availability, and defend those choices in design review

- Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software,, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products

- Work with test engineering to help define and execute functional and environmental and EMI test plans

- Incorporate manufacturability and testability feedback from build engineers into your systems

- Help evaluate existing Amca designs for opportunities to improve reliability and reduce cost

- Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments, active deployments, and customer-operated hardware

- Concurrently manage involvement in multiple projects at various stages

- Present your project and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship

Basic Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, engineering physics, or a related field

- Returning to school in Fall 2027, or graduating in Spring 2027 and interested in a full-time role. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester

- Ability to commit to a full-time, in-person 10-week internship in one of our offices in Summer 2027

- Completed coursework in circuits, electronics, or signals, and a working understanding of first principles across power, filtering, and logic

- Hands-on electrical design experience through coursework, a student project team, personal projects, or a prior internship

- Familiarity with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, debuggers, and current probes, and test automation

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience with Altium Designer or equivalent electronic design automation tools

- Experience with circuit simulation, component selection, and de-rating

- Experience on a student project team building electronics for physical hardware, such as rocketry, Formula SAE, CubeSat, or robotics

- Familiarity with DO-160, MIL-STD-810 or other qualification and certification frameworks

- Exceptionally curious and a fast learner, able to contribute across diverse part categories and manufacturing processes

- Demonstrated ability to use engineering first principles to challenge and simplify requirements

- Hands-on and practical, comfortable building, testing, and troubleshooting in real-world environments

- Thrives with ownership and takes initiative without waiting to be directed

Additional Requirements

- This internship is on-site in El Segundo, California.

- Occasional travel to vendors or other Amca sites may be required

Hourly Pay Range

$30—$50 USD

You will work alongside software engineers, architects, and AI specialists to bring up new training workloads, analyze performance bottlenecks, and develop innovative tooling that improves scalability, efficiency, and developer productivity.

- We will involve you in developing and optimizing large-scale AI training and fine-tuning workloads running on AMD GPU platforms.
- You will help bring up newly released foundation models and training frameworks, adapting implementations and training recipes for AMD hardware while establishing reproducible correctness and performance baselines.
- We will work with you to profile and analyze AI workloads, identifying bottlenecks across GPUs, CPUs, memory systems, networking, and communication infrastructure.
- You will develop tools and workflows that automate training setup, debugging, performance analysis, and optimization using LLM-powered agents and agentic AI techniques.
- You will investigate and implement optimization strategies that improve training throughput, GPU utilization, memory efficiency, and scalability across distributed multi-GPU environments.
- We will expose you to advanced profiling and performance analysis tools to benchmark and tune AI frameworks, libraries, SDKs, and applications running on AMD platforms.
- You will collaborate with software engineers and architects to evaluate emerging AI models, distributed training techniques, and performance optimization opportunities.
- Your work will help transform successful experiments into reusable workflows, best practices, and software improvements that enhance out-of-the-box AI training performance on AMD hardware.

- Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline.
- Strong programming experience in Python and/or C++.

- Distributed training systems
- Data, tensor, pipeline, expert, or context parallelism
- GPU performance optimization
- AI systems software
- High-performance computing (HPC)

- Agentic AI or LLM-powered automation

- Publications in AI, Machine Learning, High Performance Computing, Computer Architecture, or related research areas are a plus.

About the SambaNova Summer Internship Program

At SambaNova, our internship program is designed to give you hands-on experience tackling meaningful engineering challenges with real product impact. The compiler team at SambaNova powers the RDU through a unique compilation strategy. By fusing kernels into dataflow graphs that run across the entire accelerator architecture, we avoid sequential kernel launches and eliminate the memory traffic that bottlenecks conventional hardware. This is a key differentiator and unlike any other product on the market.

As a Compiler Engineer Intern, you'll work on a scoped project in a core area of our compiler, such as the IR and pass infrastructure, model lowering and partitioning, tensor tiling, memory management, or mapping operations onto the fabric. You'll write real code in C++ and Python, debug at a low level, and work with the runtime and hardware teams. A dedicated mentor and senior engineers will review your code and guide you through your project.

- Implement and test passes in the compiler's IR and pass infrastructure Help lower and partition machine learning models for execution on the RDU Contribute to tensor tiling and memory management for on-chip memory Explore how operations are mapped onto the RDU fabric to improve model performance
